# bumble:futurespace — Full Content Summary

> Coding & robotics courses for kids 8–14 using the mbot2 platform. Hands-on programming, real hardware, small groups. Powered by bumble:education.

We teach kids to code by building real robots. Not screen simulations — physical mbot2 robots they assemble, program, and watch roll across the floor. Two courses, two skill levels, one goal: the grin on a kid's face when their creation actually works.

---

## Course Catalog

### Robot Explorer — Beginner · Block Coding

**Ages:** 8–10 | **Duration:** 8 weeks, 1×/week, 60–75 min | **Price:** €25 | **Start:** 2026-10-01

**Prerequisites:** None. This is the entry-level course — kids need zero coding or robotics experience.

**What's included:** All materials, instruction, and the mbot2 robot to keep.

**Booking:** https://pretix.eu/bumbleedu/robot-explorer/

No blank-page fear here — a friendly first robot, big colorful blocks, and the moment it finally moves because of something they built.

**What kids do:**
- Build an mbot2 robot from parts (sensors, motors, controller board)
- Learn coding through colorful drag-and-drop blocks (Scratch-like)
- Program the robot to follow lines, avoid obstacles, and respond to sensors
- Debug, iterate, and celebrate when their creation works

**Learning outcomes:**
- Logic & sequencing — understanding how steps create behavior
- Loops & conditionals — making decisions in code
- Line-following robot — a working creation they take home pride in

**Final project:** A line-following mbot2 that navigates a track autonomously.

---

### Code the Machine — Intermediate · Python

**Ages:** 11–14 | **Duration:** 10 weeks, 1×/week, 90 min | **Price:** €40 | **Start:** 2026-10-01

**Prerequisites:** None required, but Robot Explorer is a natural stepping stone. Kids with some block coding experience will feel at home; complete beginners can still succeed.

**What's included:** All materials, instruction, and the mbot2 robot to keep.

**Booking:** https://pretix.eu/bumbleedu/code-the-machine/

For kids ready to trade blocks for real code — and the pride of watching a program they wrote actually drive a robot through a maze.

**What kids do:**
- Transition from visual blocks to real Python (text-based programming)
- Work with sensors: ultrasonic (distance), infrared (line following), light (ambient detection)
- Program autonomous behavior — decision-making in code
- Compete in maze challenges with their robots

**Learning outcomes:**
- Real Python code — text-based programming they can show friends
- Sensors & IoT — reading the physical world through code
- Autonomous maze robot — a robot that navigates on its own

**Final project:** An autonomous maze-navigating robot that solves a course without human input.

---

## How It Works

Three steps from curious to capable:

1. **Build** — Snap the mbot2 together and wire up the sensors. Physical hardware, real connections.
2. **Code** — Drag blocks or write Python to tell the robot what to do. From visual programming to real syntax.
3. **Go** — Hit run and watch your ideas roll across the floor. Debug, iterate, succeed.

---

## Why This Works

- **Small groups** — Every kid gets a robot, a coach's attention, and room to ask questions. No dumb questions here.
- **Real hardware** — Not a screen simulation. A robot they can hold, that listens to them.
- **No experience needed** — Everyone starts at zero and leaves further than they expected.
- **Parents included** — You see the wins as they happen, plus a real showcase to watch them show off.
- **All materials included** — The course price covers everything. Kids keep their robot.

---

## The Team

### Chris — IT Nerd · Patient Explainer

Our IT nerd with a teacher's patience: he knows every screw in the mbot2 and explains code until it finally clicks. When a kid says "I built that!", his day is made.

### Jördis — Team Soul · Heart of the Group

Our team soul: she reads the room in seconds, knows who needs a nudge and who needs quiet, and turns a bunch of kids into a real team. Every kid leaves feeling seen.

## Booking

Courses are booked through pretix at https://pretix.eu/bumbleedu/. Each course runs for a fixed term with a fixed group. Prices include all materials — kids keep their robots.

| Course | Price | Duration | Booking Link |
|--------|-------|----------|--------------|
| Robot Explorer | €25 | 8 weeks | https://pretix.eu/bumbleedu/robot-explorer/ |
| Code the Machine | €40 | 10 weeks | https://pretix.eu/bumbleedu/code-the-machine/ |

---

## About

bumble:futurespace is the education label of bumbleflies — a Munich-based team that believes kids learn best by building real things with real hardware. We run small-group coding and robotics courses using the mbot2 platform, combining hands-on building with progressive programming challenges.
